messages:
Maria (infra): kicking off Pulumi <-> Terraform integration for new region 'region-alpha' (gpuprospector). goal: provision GPU node pool + private control plane + shared infra. I'm going to create remote state + locks first, then wire CI. pinging @Jin @Priya for CI and KMS checks.

Jin: SGTM. what's the S3 bucket name and KMS key policy we should use? also need to know TF workspace name.

Priya: propose names: s3://rwinf-region-alpha-state, dynamodb table rwinf-region-alpha-lock, pulumi stack pul-region-alpha. KMS: alias/rwinf/region-alpha.

Alex: note: Pulumi currently uses self-managed backend in some regions. if we want parity we should use S3+DynamoDB+KMS for TF and Pulumi backend-v2 (s3) to keep state collocated.

Priya: quick commands I'm going to run locally:
```bash
# create tf backend artifacts
aws s3api create-bucket --bucket rwinf-region-alpha-state --region eu-north-2
aws dynamodb create-table --table-name rwinf-region-alpha-lock --attribute-definitions AttributeName=LockID,AttributeType=S --key-schema AttributeName=LockID,KeyType=HASH --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST
# kms alias
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/rwinf/region-alpha --target-key-id <key-id>
```

Maria (infra): thanks. I'll open the PR for terraform modules -> module path: infra/regions/region-alpha. Terraform vars: `region_name`, `vpc_cidr`, `gpu_count`, `instance_type`. Starting small for now.

deploy-bot: pipeline #786 started: terraform plan (infra/regions/region-alpha) triggered by Maria.

ops-bot: quota-check: GPUs requested = 40, quota available in eu-north-2 = 20. ACTION: quota increase required or reduce initial capacity.

Kate: cost note — starting at 40 GPUs will be ~120k/month (rough estimate). recommend start with 8-12 for smoke then scale.

Maria (infra): lowering initial `gpu_count` to 8 in TF vars and re-run plan. pushing update to branch `region-alpha/provision-2026`. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/region-alpha/pull/42

Jin: CI wiring notes: we need two jobs: `region-alpha/tf-apply` (protected), and `region-alpha/pulumi-apply`. Both need manual approval gate. Add step to verify KMS access using role `infra-deployers`.

Priya: adding validation step to CI: `./scripts/validate-region.sh region-alpha` — checks: VPC peering routes, MTU, node userdata success, kubelet health, NVidia driver install status.

Alex: inline snippet for validation output we expect:
```text
CHECK VPC: OK
CHECK ROUTES: OK
CHECK GPU DRIVERS: OK
KUBE NODES READY: 8/8
```

deploy-bot: pulumi stack `pul-region-alpha` started apply (job 791). watch logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/791/log

ops-bot: reminder: ensure private control plane endpoint inside VPC + control plane logs forwarded to central logging (stack name: rwinf-logging-region-alpha).

Priya: found a networking hiccup during apply: mtu mismatch on peering -> pods with jumbo frames dropped. quick fix was to set MTU=9000 on Egress gateway. pushing patch to TF route-module.

Maria (infra): resolved the MTU change, re-applied. Pulumi reported no drift. running validation now.

Jin: validations passing except one intermittent driver install on node-07. I triggered node reprovision (drain -> reprovision -> uncordon).

Kate: once node reprovision completes, please capture cost burn rate for first 72 hours and share in #finance. tag me.

Alex: small follow-up: add terraform outputs to the runbook with S3 bucket ARN, dynamodb table ARN, pulumi stack url, and CI job IDs.

Maria (infra): Handoff checklist (final) — all items are green:
- remote state S3: s3://rwinf-region-alpha-state
- lock table: rwinf-region-alpha-lock
- KMS alias: alias/rwinf/region-alpha
- TF workspace: region-alpha-prod
- Pulumi stack: pul-region-alpha (self-managed backend)
- CI jobs: 786 (tf-plan), 789 (tf-apply), 791 (pulumi-apply)
- validation script: ./scripts/validate-region.sh region-alpha
- runbook: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/region-alpha-provisioning

Maria (infra): moving thread to `ready-for-ops`. tagging @Kate for cost sign-off and @Alex for runbook grooming. :white_check_mark:

Kate: approved. good job everyone. :party_parrot:
